newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Plans to double Jewish settlements, Peace Now says.
newsitem.headline: Plans to double Jewish settlements, Peace Now says.

text.p: Israel's Peace Now group said on Tuesday in a report sure to enrage Palestinians that settlers planned to double the number of houses for Jews in the occupied West Bank.
Peace Now said 44,089 units were being planned.
"(It is) the same number of units which currently exists in all the settlements together today," Israel's largest peace group said in a statement.
It said no plan had yet received final approval, but that 16,106 units were at the stage where all that was left was for Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai to approve them.
Settler leaders denied the report and a spokesman for Mordechai, the cabinet member who authorises construction in Jewish settlements, said "the facts and figures are, to say the least, incorrect".
Left-wing legislator Ran Cohen said the meaning of such plans would be "a complete and total blow-up of the peace process".
Cohen told Israel Radio the plans were kept secret "so that the Israeli public will not know that this government is talking about peace, but planning for war".

Since coming to power in June 1996, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government has approved building of 9,500 new units in settlements, including the new 6,500-unit settlement it launched in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Settler spokesman Aharon Domb told the radio: "Peace Now typically exaggerates data...Someone fell on his head and they built on completely incorrect data."
The settler council Yesha said in a statement:

"While Peace Now's prevarication is intended to provoke international pressures on Israel's democratically elected government, the Yesha Council will continue to lobby for the...growth of Yesha's Jewish communities which in the end will exceed even the artificial numbers of Peace Now."
Neither Domb nor the council said how many units were being planned.
Peace Now's report said the Benjamin Regional Council, which is responsible for settlement in the north of the West Bank, had 44,089 units in various stages of planning.

Peace Now said that of the six planning stages required before Mordechai's signature, 8,782 units were in the initial stages; 7,026 units were in the fourth stage; 12,175 were at the fifth stage, and 16,106 were at stage six.
It based its report on Housing Ministry and settler leaks.
More than 130,000 Jews have settled amidst two million Palestinians in the territories occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. Most live in the West Bank.
Palestinians want to establish an independent state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with East Jerusalem as capital. They say settlement pre-empts final peace talks.
Peace talks ground to a halt when Israel began the 6,500-unit settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
A U.S. effort to revive negotiations was set back last week when two Islamic militants committed a double suicide bombing that killed 13 people and wounded 170 at an Israeli market.
